Q1: 1,3-Butadiene is associated with known hazards (Tier 1) for carcinogenicity, mutagenicity, reproductive hazards (CMR), and organ/systemic hazards (OGN). Current scientific data also suggests potential hazards (Tier 2) for environmental (ENV), inhalation (IHL), and dermal/eye (SKN) exposures. While oral hazards (ORL) are considered low to moderate, there is insufficient data to assess endocrine disruption (EDC).
Q2: 1,3-Butadiene is recognized as a significant chemical of concern by multiple prominent bodies, including its classification as a known human carcinogen (IARC Group 1) and its inclusion on California's Proposition 65 list. It is also identified as a hazardous air pollutant and a potential endocrine disruptor.
Q3: 1,3-Butadiene is extensively characterized, supported by over 55,000 scientific references, far exceeding the median for similar chemicals. Its molecular formula is precisely defined, and it is classified as a well-understood 'Small Molecule,' indicating a complete and thoroughly studied hazard profile despite a specific data gap for endocrine disruption.
